obligations.statement: Every operation round-trips: a serialized envelope deserializes to an equal value
A verb payload carried in a response envelope is byte-identical to the bare FR-031 payload the facade serializes, per verb
A verb request nested in an envelope is validated against the FR-031 schema before any project data is read
A response payload tagged with a verb other than the one requested is refused rather than returned
An envelope the backend cannot interpret is refused with a registered `SVC_BACKEND_PROTOCOL_MISMATCH` corrective envelope
A client and backend at different contract revisions refuse at handshake rather than coercing
Progress reaches a client as chunk frames ahead of the final answer, terminated by one end frame
A verb request carries whether chunked delivery was asked for; absent is false and is serialized as absent, and a non-boolean is refused as a protocol mismatch
A session request returns a session handle, container id, scope, and document prefix
Scope rebinding and document prefixing are applied by the backend, not by any client
An unresolvable project root is refused with `SVC_BACKEND_SESSION_INVALID` before a container is created
A verb call naming no session is served against the sole binding when exactly one is held, and refused as ambiguous when several are
Two sessions on one container share a single runtime rather than each paying migration
A session request declares whether an absent container may be seeded, and a request that forbids seeding is refused rather than answered from a guess
A client reaches an embedded backend by direct invocation, serializing nothing
A client reaches a daemon over the endpoint and completes a call
A refusal crosses the endpoint as a corrective envelope, not a closed connection
An endpoint with nothing behind it is refused with `SVC_BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE`
A second backend finding a live endpoint refuses rather than displacing the first
A client that finds a published descriptor connects to it in preference to embedding a backend of its own
Every client surface satisfies AC-6 — the CLI, the MCP server, the control surface, and the Desktop Shell alike

Liveness — for discovery and for bind contention — means the daemon answered the health operation reporting a reachable database within the probe deadline; a daemon that accepts connections but reports its database unreachable, or does not answer, is not live

A starting daemon finding the endpoint held by an owner whose database is unreachable takes over: `SIGTERM` to the pid named by the bind lock, a bounded wait for the endpoint's release, then the claim — and ends up serving with its descriptor published
An unhealthy owner that does not release the endpoint within the bounded wait is refused to, with an error naming its pid; it is never `SIGKILL`ed
Reindex is invocable from any front door holding a user or tool session, refused for agent sessions, and reports failure with a registered code
Index settings written through the contract are read back through it and applied to verb calls from every client
An operation the backend does not yet serve refuses with a registered code naming why, rather than returning a default
Database status reports the running server, whether the backend started or attached to it, and the resolved bundle, and carries no connection string
Every client reporting on database readiness answers from this operation, so no surface reports from its own environment

Schema status reports `ready: true` against a migrated database, `ready: false` with no detail for a determined-absent schema — without materializing the schema as a side effect of asking — and `ready: false` with a leading diagnostic-code detail when undetermined
Health reports a reachable database as reachable with no detail, and an unreachable one as unreachable with a leading diagnostic-code detail — never free text with a connection string at its head
An agent session cannot enroll a plan
An agent session cannot reach any operation on the backend itself
An agent session can reconcile an already-enrolled plan
A missing tracker credential is refused distinctly from a missing grant, so a token problem is not mistaken for a permissions problem

A sealed settings document is verified by the Backend module against key material only it holds, and a forged, tampered, or internally inconsistent document is refused there — not only by the client that presented it
A sealed session remains agent-authorized when its connected client claims a broader transport actor kind
The reported state is derived from a completed connection, not from the presence of a descriptor file
An absent descriptor reports not running
A descriptor with nothing behind it reports not responding, distinctly from not running
Starting a backend with no desktop app produces a listening backend the surface then observes as running
A start request against a live backend is refused rather than displacing or racing it
A stop request ends the running backend, and the next observation reports it stopped

With a backend running and no desktop app, the surface lists every registry entry with its resolution state, project count, watcher status, and last sync run, sourced from the backend's status operations

A per-entry stop control halts change-driven reindex for that root and the listing shows it stopped; the start control resumes it and one reindex picks up interim edits (FR-105-AC-5 through this surface)
With no backend running, the surface presents no registry listing and no watcher controls
A backend with no external connection string and no desktop application present starts a server from the shared bundle directory and serves a verb call against it
Bundle resolution follows the stated order, and an explicit argument outranks both the shared directory and packaged resources
A backend with neither a bundle nor an external connection string refuses to start with a corrective envelope naming how to install one
A client disconnecting, and every client disconnecting, leaves the server running
A backend that attached to an externally supplied database leaves it running when it stops
A backend starting against a data directory a live backend already serves refuses, rather than attaching to its server
A backend finding a healthy server whose owning backend is gone adopts it rather than starting a second
A backend given an external connection string starts no server of its own
With a daemon already running, opening the shell yields one backend process, and the shell's verb calls are served by it
With no daemon running, the shell starts one, connects to it, and serves a verb call
The shell's dependency closure carries no backend, driver, or ORM crate, and no embedded-backend feature
A start that fails surfaces a corrective envelope rather than a degraded mode
Quitting the shell leaves the backend and its database serving other clients
A daemon started with a populated registry and no connected client composes the workspace and creates the workspace container record, observable through the registry status operation
Stopping and restarting the daemon yields the same served workspace roots, derived from the persisted registry with no dependence on prior sessions
A registry edit saved while the daemon is serving takes effect — an added root's projects become servable and a removed root's stop being composed — with no daemon restart
A persisted legacy `dev_dir` with no `workspace_roots` list is read as the single-entry registry containing it, matching the FR-070 migration
An absent or unreadable registry yields the default `~/dev` registry, a recorded condition, and a daemon that still serves
The registry status operation reports every configured root with its resolution state and project count, and carries no connection string or secret material

With a daemon serving and no client ever connected, editing a Markdown artifact under a configured root results in a completed workspace reindex whose graph reflects the edit, observable by a CLI query afterward — the desktop application never runs
A change batch's edits are reflected in verb answers after the next completed reindex, and answers never regress to a state older than the most recently completed run
A session bind issued after a change but before the covering reindex completes succeeds without blocking, and a repeat query after the run completes reflects the change
Restarting the daemon re-establishes watches from the persisted registry and one scheduled reindex picks up edits made while it was down

A contract stop request halts change-driven reindex for that root — its status reads stopped and edits trigger no run — while its indexed graph stays served; a start request resumes watching and one reindex picks up the interim edits
A project whose watch cannot be established is recorded with a stable error code in the watcher status while the remaining projects stay watched
Clients connecting and disconnecting — including every client disconnecting — leaves the watches running
Repeated liveness questions about a healthy endpoint within the reuse window cost one health exchange in total, not one each
Repeated liveness questions about an endpoint whose probe failed are answered from the record within the backoff window, without a further connection
Consecutive non-healthy verdicts widen the backoff window geometrically and stop widening at the stated ceiling
A descriptor naming a different process id or address is probed afresh regardless of any recorded verdict
Discarding the record for an endpoint causes the next question to probe
A host asked to ensure a backend is running returns a recorded healthy endpoint without spawning a daemon
An endpoint identity carrying no process id is re-probed on every non-healthy question, while its healthy verdicts are still reused
The control surface reports a daemon that answers health with an unreachable database as unhealthy, never as running
The control surface's start action starts a candidate against an unhealthy owner and reports the resulting healthy backend
The control surface's start action still refuses while the owner is healthy
The Desktop Shell's backend report distinguishes an unhealthy daemon from a running and from a non-responding one
Client discovery refuses an unhealthy daemon with `SVC_BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE` and a corrective naming the unreachable database, rather than returning a handle
The MCP configuration view renders the unhealthy and incompatible daemon states with their own copy
Every reported backend state states whether starting and whether stopping is the sensible next action, and no state offers both starting a second backend and a healthy owner
A daemon that completes the handshake announcing a contract revision this build does not speak is classified incompatible, not unresponsive, and both revisions are recorded
A starting daemon finding an incompatible owner refuses, naming the owner's pid and both revisions, and sends it no signal
Client discovery against an incompatible owner refuses with `SVC_BACKEND_PROTOCOL_MISMATCH` naming both revisions
The control surface reports an incompatible owner distinctly and offers no start while it holds the endpoint
A host asked to ensure a backend is running refuses against an incompatible owner without spawning a daemon
A non-empty runtime-directory override resolves the descriptor path in preference to the platform default, on macOS, Linux, and Windows alike
An empty override resolves exactly what an unset override resolves
Descriptor, socket, and bind lock resolve under the same runtime directory, so no override can split them
Every spawn that redirects a child to an isolated home clears the override for that child

A descriptor published by a serving backend carries a configuration fingerprint with both a build identity and a database identity, alongside the endpoint, pid, and protocol version it already carried, and the build identity distinguishes two builds of one package version

Two backends configured against the same connection target publish equal database identities; two configured against different targets — including targets that differ only in a target-selecting query parameter — publish different ones
Connection strings differing only in user name, password, or connection-tuning parameters yield the same database identity, and no credential substring appears anywhere in the published descriptor
Comparing a published fingerprint with an expected one classifies it as matching, build-mismatched, database-mismatched, or unknown, with no connection opened
A descriptor lacking a configuration fingerprint still yields its endpoint, process id, and contract revision, and classifies as unknown — never as a match
A reader that finds a mismatch reports it and leaves the other process running
A host that cannot reach a backend names the incumbent's endpoint, process id, and contract revision, and classifies its build, rather than reporting only that nothing became reachable
A backend refused the endpoint by a live owner names the owner's process id and how its published configuration differs from the refused starter's own
A verb call failing with a backend-unreachable condition leaves no cached session behind
The call after a discarded session binds a fresh session and is served by the backend then listening, with no application restart
A verb call refused on its merits leaves the cached session in place, and the next call reuses it
Discarding a session performs no bind of its own; no backend request is issued until the next call arrives
The failure returned to the renderer after an invalidating call is the backend's own envelope, and a binding held for a different scope survives the discard
A call that failed with a backend-unreachable condition is not resent by the shell

Every Desktop Shell surface that reaches the backend — verbs, reindex, projection status, plan-sync, and container reporting — does so through the invalidating rule, and no path exists to hold the cached session without it
A bind whose container has a cached runtime built against the configured database identity reuses it, building nothing
A bind arriving after the configured database identity changed discards every cached runtime and builds a fresh one
A health check reporting the database unreachable leaves no cached runtime behind
Eviction opens no connection and builds nothing; the cache is empty and the next bind is what pays
A session bound before an eviction is served after it, from a rebuilt runtime, with its identifier, authority, and grants unchanged and no second bind from the client
An eviction landing while a session is being bound leaves that session stale rather than falsely current, so its next call rebuilds
Several sessions stranded on one container by an eviction cause one runtime construction between them, not one each
The value compared to decide eviction is the FR-113 database digest, and no connection string is held outside the backend to compare
A search from a session whose scope is not a member of the composed workspace returns `RETR_NOTE_SCOPE_UNWATCHED`, whose detail names the bound scope
A search from a member scope whose container has no completed index run returns `RETR_NOTE_SCOPE_UNINDEXED`
A search from a member, indexed, non-empty scope that matches nothing returns an empty hit list carrying no coverage note
Classification follows the stated precedence and never yields two coverage states: a non-member scope reports unwatched regardless of its index state
A search that is both semantically degraded and uncovered carries the provider note and the coverage note, provider note first
A search from a covered scope that returns hits carries no coverage note
A search from a session bound before the workspace composition resolved carries no coverage note
A member scope whose completed index run left no document under the session's bound document prefix returns `RETR_NOTE_SCOPE_EMPTY`, and a member prefix holding documents classifies covered
A container with a recorded index completion still classifies covered while a subsequent index run is in progress
CLI `search --json` is field-equivalent to MCP `search` for the same request per the FR-031 relation
CLI `links --json` and `history --json` are field-equivalent to MCP `links` and `history` for the same requests per the FR-031 relation
With the `markup` tool granted, CLI `markup --json` is field-equivalent to the MCP `markup` tool for the same request per the FR-031 relation
The same failing request through both transports yields the identical FR-030 `code` and `corrective` field values
Both transports reach every shared verb through one service implementation; neither contains transport-local verb logic
`filament-mcp` answers initialize and tool-listing requests over stdio, enumerating exactly `search`, `links`, and `history` plus the tools granted by the effective generated settings

With markup granted, the `markup` tool is enumerated and serves FR-014 markup operations; with markup not granted, it is absent from enumeration and calling it returns an error without any service dispatch
Successful tool results carry the FR-031 service response payload with no fields added, renamed, dropped, or type-coerced
Ambiguous and unsupported targets return the FR-030 envelope with `SVC_TARGET_AMBIGUOUS` / `SVC_TARGET_UNSUPPORTED` and unmodified `corrective` fields, and no target data is read
A tool call whose selector `scope_id` differs from the bound project scope returns `SVC_SCOPE_CROSS_PROJECT` with no target data read
Every tool call dispatches through the FR-014 service verbs with a trusted agent actor reference; the server contains no transport-local verb logic and no direct database access
With no reachable backend, `filament-mcp` exits 2 with a diagnostic naming the missing prerequisite (a reachable backend) and writes no MCP response to stdout
Tool arguments accept an optional `format` alongside `target` and `params`, declared in the tool's `inputSchema`; any other top-level argument is still refused
All four subcommands construct FR-031 `VerbRequest`s from their arguments and dispatch them through the FR-014 service verbs
Default output is human-readable; `--json` writes exactly one JSON document to stdout with diagnostics on stderr
`--json` output conforms to the FR-031 response schema for its verb with no fields added, renamed, dropped, or type-coerced
A failing verb emits the FR-030 envelope and exits 1; a usage error exits 2 without dispatching a verb; success exits 0
The command surface exposes no option naming fusion weights, similarity thresholds, or embedding budgets
Inside a project, the resolved scope equals the canonical FR-021 scope of the nearest marker ancestor; outside any project, the command exits 2 without dispatch
The default `links` rendering names both endpoints of every edge, grouped by relationship kind, and states truncation as its own statement
The default rendering is produced by the shared [FR-117](./FR-117-compact-markdown-output.md) renderer; the CLI declares no rendering of its own
A launch yields a `created` session; attach transitions it to `attached`; a typed input round-trips through the PTY and returns as a typed output event
A typed resize changes the PTY dimensions observed by the agent process; a typed stop terminates the process and leaves the session `stopped`
Detach keeps the process alive in `detached` with output buffered within the 1 MiB bound; reattach — from the main window or a popout — replays the buffer and resumes live events
Project switch, the FR-003 markup bake-completion event, and application quit each stop every session of the affected project scope, leaving zero agent session processes
Commands invalid for the session's state (input or resize after `stopped`, attach to `stopped`) return typed `AGT_SESSION_STOPPED` errors with no side effects

An unsupported agent kind with an allowlisted deep link dispatches through the shell's FR-017 external-URL launcher; a link the outbound-launch allowlist refuses yields `AGT_LINK_NOT_ALLOWLISTED` with no dispatch
The renderer-facing session surface consists of typed commands and events only; no interface returns a raw PTY handle or file descriptor or spawns a shell for the renderer

A spawned agent process's environment contains only the explicit inheritance allowlist — `PATH` inherited as-is, no database connection string, resolved secret, or credential-bearing variable — and its working directory is the project root of the session's scope
An attach command against an already-`attached` session is refused with a typed `AGT_ALREADY_ATTACHED` error and the existing attachment continues uninterrupted
After a simulated app crash with a live session, the next shell startup detects and terminates the orphaned agent process, leaving zero orphans

A scan reads only the dev directory's immediate children plus each child's own entry list, and never descends further regardless of child contents
A `dev_dir` pointing at a nonexistent directory and one pointing at an unreadable directory each yield an empty registry and no scan failure
Registration alone confers no filesystem access: an FR-018 read under a discovered but unopened project is refused
Dropping the currently open project from the registry leaves the selected project root and its authorization grants unchanged
A main-window focus regain triggers a discovery scan: a project added on disk while the window was unfocused appears in the registry after focus, with a projects-changed event and no manual refresh

An entry whose canonical directory path persists across a rescan keeps its opaque registry id, so a rendered switcher id stays resolvable and a background rescan yields no spurious `SHELL_ROOT_REFUSED`
Rapid repeated main-window focus regains within the minimum interval trigger at most one discovery rescan
When two scans overlap across a disk change, the scan reading the later directory state wins and a stale earlier read never overwrites the newer registry
A symlinked child registers its canonical target path, and two children resolving to the same canonical path register a single entry (first in directory-name order)

The settings panel exposes an editable workspace-root control (the [FR-070](./FR-070-configurable-workspace-roots.md) roots editor; a legacy `dev_dir` shows as its migrated single entry); changing the root and saving through the ordinary settings path rescans the new directory and retargets the switcher without a reload
The switcher lists exactly the registry's projects and updates after a projects-changed event without a reload

With discovery active, the explicit dialog open of a project outside the dev directory sets that project as the root exactly as before
A switcher open while another project is open stops the old root's watches and rebases handling onto the new root per FR-019
The generated switcher-open binding carries a registry-entry reference only, with no renderer-supplied path field

A dev directory with three marker-bearing repositories produces one workspace container whose graph contains nodes from every repository, each node attributable to its source repository by its path prefix

Markdown outside a project's `spec/`, `plan/`, or `reviews/` (a top-level `README.md`, a `docs/` tree, a `node_modules` subtree), a markerless child, and a dot-prefixed child each contribute no nodes to the workspace graph
A repository added to the registry gains graph nodes on the next reindex, and a repository removed from the registry loses its nodes on the next reindex
A renderer FR-018 read under a repository that is indexed but not opened is refused
Opening a project through the FR-067 switcher leaves the workspace graph spanning every discovered project and does not narrow it to the opened project
An unset `dev_dir` and an empty registry each yield an empty workspace graph with a recorded run and no failure
After a reindex, the graph sync monitor snapshot reports the workspace root and the count of indexed projects
Two repositories that each define an artifact with the same code (e.g. both `FR-001`) produce two distinct graph nodes in the workspace container, neither overwriting the other
An `ix://` link from an artifact in one registered repository to an artifact in another registered repository resolves to a graph edge between their nodes in the single workspace container

Two repositories that each define an artifact with the same code (e.g. both `FR-001`) produce two distinct `artifacts` projection rows, each scoped to its own repository `specs` row, with neither discarded as a duplicate

A link whose target cannot be resolved to a projection node is recorded as an unresolved-edge entry surfaced through the reindex summary — never silently dropped and never guessed onto a same-code artifact in a repository the link did not name — and a later run in which the target becomes resolvable produces the edge and clears the record without re-extracting the source
A re-extraction that re-mints a document's graph nodes under a new repository identity retires the old-identity node and edge rows in the same run, leaving exactly the current extraction's nodes

A document carrying a frontmatter `id` but no `object:` declaration (the shape of every spec artifact) yields a primary artifact graph node named by that id, and its frontmatter relationship links persist as graph edges between artifact nodes

An extracted edge whose source cannot be bound to a projection node is recorded as an unresolved-edge entry — never silently dropped — and a later run in which the source becomes bindable produces the edge and clears the record; no code path discards an extracted edge without either persisting it or recording it

A repository whose git remote names organization `acme` (e.g. `git@github.com:acme/widgets.git`) produces graph nodes and edges qualified `ix://acme/widgets/{code}` — the organization is the one read from the remote, not a hardcoded constant
A repository with no readable git remote is qualified under a clearly-flagged local marker (never under another organization's name), and its references still resolve within the workspace graph

Two repositories whose git remotes name the same repository under different organizations (e.g. `acme/api` and `other/api`) produce distinct graph nodes for the same artifact code, qualified by their differing organization segments, and an `ix://` link naming one organization resolves to exactly that organization's node rather than reporting the repository-segment collision ambiguous
Editing a Markdown artifact under any discovered project's `spec/`, `plan/`, or `reviews/` triggers exactly one coalesced workspace reindex
A change outside any discovered project's `spec/`, `plan/`, or `reviews/` — a markerless directory, or a non-artifact subdirectory — triggers no workspace reindex
A project added to the registry gains `spec/`, `plan/`, and `reviews/` watches, and a project dropped from the registry has its watches stopped, after the reconciling scan
A burst of edits across several repositories within the debounce window coalesces into one workspace reindex run, and triggers arriving during an in-flight run coalesce into at most one follow-up run

With the registry's handle demand above the platform ceiling, projects are admitted to native watching in directory-name order for as long as each one's cost fits, registered handles never exceed the ceiling, and the count left in neither tier is recorded
The manual workspace-reindex command schedules a reindex and is refused with a stable error code while a run is in flight

While code indexing is enabled, a save to an allowlisted source file under a discovered project joins the change batch and its repository's source directories are watched; with code indexing disabled the same save joins no batch and no source directory is watched
A project not admitted to native watching is placed in the polled tier, and a Markdown change under it is delivered within the Markdown poll interval rather than waiting for a full reindex
Markdown and source polling run on their own intervals, and the polled tier registers no source directory unless both code indexing and the source poll interval are enabled
The polled tier holds no more than its project and directory bounds; projects past them are recorded as being in neither tier
With both poll intervals absent, no poll watcher is created and unadmitted projects are left to full reindex alone

A workspace configured with a marker-bearing root and a markerless dev-directory root produces one registry whose projects are the single repository plus every marker-bearing child of the dev directory, each attributable to its source repository
A persisted legacy `dev_dir` with no `workspace_roots` migrates to the single-entry list `[dev_dir]`, and the resulting workspace container identity equals the pre-migration FR-068 dev_dir container
Saving an added workspace root rescans and schedules a reindex that gains the added root's projects' nodes, and removing a root loses on the next reindex exactly the projects contributed only by it
A project reachable through two configured roots registers as a single deduplicated entry, and the workspace container identity is independent of the order of the configured roots
An FR-018 read under a directory that is a configured workspace root but is not opened is refused
Root resolution and classification run only in Rust: the renderer receives project metadata through commands and push events and never enumerates a root

Adding the currently open project — whose root is covered by no configured root — appends its root to `workspace_roots` and brings its nodes into the workspace graph on the next sync; a request for an already-covered directory is a no-op
A configured root that is absent, unreadable, or contributes no classified project yields an empty contribution and no scan failure, and the other roots' projects still register

Two distinct repositories under different roots that share a directory basename each receive a distinct repository scope, so an artifact code they both define persists as two distinct rows rather than collapsing under one scope
Selecting the graph menu item emits `filament-graph-open` and the main pane switches to the graph mode
The in-app toggle enters the graph mode and returning restores the spec preview with prior artifact selection intact
"Show in graph" enters the mode focused on the active artifact's node
"Open artifact" from a node detail panel leaves the mode and opens that artifact in the spec preview; a node without an addressable target shows the action disabled
With no project open, the graph mode shows an empty state and issues no verb requests
The "show in graph" control renders in the artifact preview header as an icon control named for the action, with a glyph distinct from the graph-mode toggle
Loaded graph data renders exactly once per node and edge: the project view accumulates every `graph_export` page with progress against totals, and a focus target renders its `links` neighborhood
Pan, zoom, and fit-to-view controls operate on the rendered scene
Hover highlights the node and its incident edges and dims non-incident elements
Selecting a node opens a detail panel with the node's label, kind, and relationships grouped by edge type with inverse labels (or the `(inbound)` fallback) on inbound edges
Expanding a node merges its neighborhood into the scene without duplicate nodes
A response with `truncated: true` renders a visible truncation indicator
A failed `links` or `graph_export` request surfaces the corrective error and leaves the prior scene rendered
With WebGL unavailable, the mode shows a corrective graphics-unavailable state
The detail panel is absent until a node is selected, is dismissible, and reopens on selecting a node again — including the node that is already selected
The canvas fills the mode's pane with its controls overlaid on it, and the progress, truncation, scene-limit, and error states stay readable with every disclosure closed
At most one disclosure is open at a time, and a pointer press outside an open disclosure or Escape dismisses it without disturbing the scene

*(retired — issue 278)* Seeded-density invariance. The renderer places the scene itself and pins any point given an explicit position, so there is no seeding step whose density could be asserted; the separation guarantee it existed to serve is now stated by FR-080-AC-16
*(retired — issue 278)* Node-count-derived refinement budget. Refinement is no longer run against a wall-clock budget; settling is measured instead, and NFR-041 states that measurement

A settling indicator is visible, with every disclosure closed, while refinement runs; its stop control ends refinement without re-seeding or restarting the layout, and the indicator clears once the scene has settled. An open that renders a stored layout ([FR-124](FR-124-persisted-graph-layout.md)) runs no refinement and shows no indicator
Once refinement ends, no two rendered nodes overlap: every pair's center distance is at least the sum of their rendered radii

The settled scene leaves every pair of nodes clear of each other **in the layout model**, and the canvas background resolves from its theme token with no color literal in the graph module. The guarantee is stated over the layout; because the drawn size tracks the zoom level (FR-080-AC-32), the layout-model clearance is also the on-screen clearance whenever the zoom is at or above the size floor, and below the floor the drawn overlap of a separated pair is bounded by the floor-to-zoom ratio rather than unbounded
Where the layout cannot spread a scene at all — every node left at the same position — the nodes are still separated deterministically rather than drawn stacked on one another

A spec-layer node at rest is drawn in the categorical swatch its object type resolves to — the swatch at the type's position in the sorted object-type vocabulary modulo the swatch count — so two object types whose sorted positions differ by less than the swatch count are drawn in different colors
An object type absent from the sorted vocabulary, or whose swatch token resolves empty, is drawn in the themed default accent, never unstyled or blank
Each object type in the filter legend shows a swatch equal to the color that type's nodes are drawn in at rest

Hover emphasis outranks every static encoding: while a node is hovered it is the focus, nodes incident to it stay emphasized, and every other node is de-emphasized — regardless of the object-type swatch or code-layer accent those nodes would otherwise carry
In a scene containing both layers, every node is seeded into its own layer's region, and the regions are pairwise disjoint — no node of one layer falls within another's extent

After refinement ends, the distance between any two layers' centroids exceeds the mean distance from each of those layers' nodes to its own centroid — the groups remain separated by more than their own spread
In a scene containing both layers, each region carries an on-canvas label naming its layer, positioned over that layer's current centroid
A single-layer scene is seeded as one arrangement centered on the origin — the placement it had before layer regions existed — and shows no region labels
Region labels are measured over visible nodes only: a layer hidden entirely by the FR-082 filters contributes no region, and a scene left with one visible layer shows no labels
The mode offers a cluster axis — none, repository, layer, object type, or community — with exactly one active at a time, and reports the active axis and the number of groups it produced
Community clustering groups nodes by the loaded graph's own connectivity, recovering distinct connected groups rather than one undifferentiated group or one group per node

A node the active axis cannot place — an unconnected node under community clustering, a placeholder endpoint under object-type clustering — is reported as ungrouped and receives no group placement, rather than being assigned a group of its own or a shared catch-all
Cluster assignment is recomputed when a load completes and when the axis changes, and not per accumulated page; the assignment is reproducible across runs over one unchanged scene

A node carries a label when the reader is hovering it, has selected it, or is focused on it, and carries none otherwise, whatever the scene's size; a drawn label is positioned with the node it names and follows it as the camera moves, and a cluster region is labelled by a human-readable name rather than an internal group key

Except while a scene is settling, the multiplier applied to every node's drawn size equals the camera's zoom level clamped to a fixed floor and ceiling, so between those bounds a node's screen radius is its layout radius times the zoom — the layout-model separation of FR-080-AC-16 made visible — and a fitted whole-project scene never draws its nodes as one merged mass. While a scene is settling the multiplier is held at the value it carried when settling began and does not follow the camera

Repository clustering keys each node on the org and repo segments of its `ix://` identity, by the same qualification rule the indexer's reference parser applies; a ref with fewer than three segments after the scheme, or an identity that is not an `ix://` ref, is reported as ungrouped

When the active axis produces more than one group, every group is assigned an explicit cluster centre, the centres are pairwise distinct, deterministic for an unchanged scene, and bounded away from the simulation-space boundary, and the assignment reaches the renderer's cluster forces

While a cluster axis with more than one group is active, a node at rest is drawn in its group's categorical swatch — the swatch at the group's position in the assignment's stable group order modulo the swatch count — and an ungrouped node keeps the fill it would have with no axis active

Link opacity scales down with the number of drawn links — full opacity at or below a fixed budget, proportional above it, floored above zero — and the link distance fade tightens on scenes above the large-scene threshold, so a whole-project scene renders structure rather than a full-opacity hairball

The whole-project view opens with the repository axis active and the focus view opens with no axis active; a scene in which the repository axis yields at most one group renders exactly as it would with no axis active

A scene that has not had its camera taken is framed automatically exactly twice in its lifetime — once when settling begins, so a freshly mounted or remounted scene is never left out of view, and once when settling ends — with no automatic camera movement in between; any user camera input (wheel, drag, the zoom controls, a recenter) ends automatic framing for that scene's lifetime, including the settle-time fit

When settling ends, the held drawn-size multiplier reaches the value the settled camera implies within a bounded interval, moving in steps no larger than half that final value, so the settle is not marked by every node changing size in one frame

While the viewport holds fewer labelled candidates than a fixed legibility bound, every candidate in it carries a label, so zooming into a region reads the names in it; at or above that bound only the nodes of FR-080-AC-31 are labelled. The bound is on the candidates on screen, not on the size of the scene
Typing produces a debounced `search` verb request and a suggestion list showing each hit's target reference and snippet
Selecting a suggestion centers the camera on the node in the loaded scene, or enters the focus view on it when not loaded
A no-hit search shows an explicit no-matches state
A failed search surfaces the corrective error and leaves the scene intact
The search control opens from a keyboard accelerator, and dismissing it returns focus to the control that opened it

A hit carrying an FR-123 locator renders its excerpt and, distinctly from it, the source path, line, and enclosing heading; a hit without a locator renders the excerpt alone with no placeholder location
A hit carrying FR-123 identity fields is named by its `code` and `title`; a hit carrying neither falls back to its target reference
The legend lists exactly the edge types in the loaded graph; toggling one shows/hides those edges in the project view and adds/removes it from the focus view's `edge_types`
Object-type toggles hide/show loaded nodes in the project view and constrain the focus view's `object_types`
The depth control spans 1–5 and a change re-requests the neighborhood at the new depth
Direction selection (in/out/both) is reflected in the request and the rendered edges
Filtering to an empty result shows a filtered-to-empty state naming the active filters

A filter disclosure reports the number of filters deviating from their defaults — the defaults being per view: the whole-project view opens with the connectivity filter engaged and the repository cluster axis active, the focus view with neither — and the filtered-to-empty state stays visible without opening it
Engaging the hide-unconnected control hides exactly the nodes with no visible edge in the project view
Disengaging the hide-unconnected control restores every node it hid
Connectedness is evaluated after the other filters: hiding the only edge type connecting a node makes that node unconnected and hides it while the control is engaged
The hide-unconnected control is disabled outside the project view
While nodes are hidden as unconnected, the scene readout reports the hidden count; while none are, it reports nothing
Hiding every node as unconnected shows the filtered-to-empty state of FR-082-AC-5, not an empty canvas
The hide-unconnected control counts toward the disclosure's active-filter count while the project view is active and the control deviates from its engaged default, and not otherwise

The whole-project view opens with the hide-unconnected control engaged and the hidden count reported; the focus view never engages it. When a view's control has not been touched by the user, its state follows the view's default across view changes; once touched, the user's choice persists
An artifact whose frontmatter declares an identifier renders a header carrying that identifier as a distinct element, the title, and the archetype icon
The body heading restating the header is absent from the rendered body, and the title appears exactly once in the pane
A document whose leading heading does not restate the header keeps that heading in the rendered body
An artifact whose identifier falls back to a file name renders a header with a title and no identifier element
The graph action is reachable by its accessible name from the header and enters the graph mode focused on the active artifact
The rendered artifact title occupies one header row at the pane's default width in both themes
A successfully loaded artifact shows no load-status message, while an unreadable artifact still shows the corrective failure message
An open path with no enumerated artifact record still renders the header and its graph action, titled from the file's base name and carrying no identifier element
Exactly one renderer entry point answers artifact impact; the inspector's blast-radius pane obtains its answer from it
An artifact whose identifier matches the canonical grammar anchors on an artifact selector; one that does not anchors on its document path
The impact result separates direct from indirect impact and labels each node with the relationship type that reached it
The impact request and the graph mode's focus request are the same bounded `links` contract
An artifact-anchored traversal resolves its roots without reading document content, against a real Postgres graph
A graph that cannot answer surfaces the corrective error rather than an empty result

A whole-project scene whose repository axis yields more than one group opens collapsed: exactly one meta-node per repository group, each identified by a `repo://{org}/{repo}` id that no real node id can collide with, labelled by the repository name, and drawn in the repository's cluster swatch
A meta-node's drawn size grows monotonically with the number of member nodes it stands for, within the same bounded size range real nodes use

Two repositories with at least one underlying edge between their members are connected by exactly one aggregate link per unordered pair, carrying the count of underlying edges as its weight, and an aggregate link's drawn width grows monotonically with its weight

Activating a repository meta-node expands it: the meta-node and its aggregate links are removed, the repository's member nodes appear with their real edges, links between an expanded node and a still-collapsed repository attach to that repository's meta-node, and every other collapsed repository remains collapsed
A repository expanded by the reader can be collapsed again from its detail affordance, restoring the meta-node presentation of FR-122-AC-1 for that repository
A search hit inside a collapsed repository expands that repository before recentring, and the hit node is present in the scene when the recenter completes

The FR-082 filters apply to the underlying graph before aggregation: a member node hidden by any filter contributes to no meta-node size and no aggregate weight, and a repository whose members are all hidden contributes no meta-node
The focus view renders without collapse, and the scene readout in the collapsed project view continues to report the underlying loaded node and edge totals rather than the meta counts

The collapsed scene derivation is pure: one unchanged (loaded graph, repository assignment, expanded set, filter state) input produces one identical derived scene, with no time- or randomness-dependent output
A whole-project scene whose repository axis yields at most one group renders without collapse, exactly as FR-080 specifies
Activating a node that is not a meta-node behaves as FR-080 specifies for that node — expansion applies to repository meta-nodes only
A second open of an unchanged corpus renders at the stored positions, reports its layout source as stored, and shows no settling indicator
Every node's position on a warm open equals the position it settled at on the cold open that stored it
The corpus key is identical for two loads of the same nodes and edges regardless of the order the pages arrived in, and differs when a node identity is added, removed, or re-pointed
Changing the layout version constant makes an open compute its layout from the seed even though a stored entry for the project exists

An open whose corpus gained a small number of nodes reports a partial layout source, places every retained identity within one layout unit of its stored position, and places each new identity near a neighbour it was loaded with rather than at the seed, spreading several new identities sharing one neighbour at constant density rather than on a single ring around it
An open whose corpus differs from the stored entry by more than the fixed fraction computes its layout from the seed and reports the computed source
A store that throws on read, throws on write, or returns an undecodable entry yields a computed layout and a rendered scene, with no error surfaced to the reader
A warm open transitions the scene into view over a bounded interval and reaches its stored positions by the end of it
The stored entry is written on every settle, including the settle that ends a partial open
An index run completing for the open project updates the rendered scene to the reloaded corpus, adding nodes the run introduced and dropping nodes it removed

Across that update the scene is never reported settling and never renders an intermediate unsettled frame: the rendered positions go from the previous settled layout to the new one and through no other arrangement

The update does not take the camera back from the reader: a scene whose camera the reader had taken is not re-framed by it, and the update writes the new positions to the store under the reloaded corpus's key
The hybrid entry point returns project-scoped lexical results when no embedding provider is configured, carrying the semantic-disabled note
Hybrid search reports lexical, vector, and recency signal contributions per hit when embeddings are available

A `folder` or `document` filter keeps artifact and graph-node hits whose owning document lies under it, drops hits outside it, and matches whole path segments so a sibling folder sharing a name prefix is not swallowed
Two artifact hits sharing a code across repositories carry identical selectors and distinct document paths, so each remains individually addressable
Neighborhoods return bounded nodes and edges
A request with empty or absent filters returns at most the default-depth (1), default-limit (100) neighborhood, never the whole graph
Unsupported and ambiguous targets return corrective errors
On the two-project fixture, cross-project targets are rejected before graph rows are read
Traversal of a cyclic neighborhood terminates, and a node reachable by multiple in-bound paths appears exactly once at its shortest-path depth
Every returned node projecting a spec artifact carries that artifact's code and title and its document's path; a node projecting neither omits those fields
A response reports the depth and limit actually applied after defaulting and clamping, and a result cut by either bound is reported as truncated
Resolving identity for a bounded neighborhood costs a fixed number of queries independent of node count, and reads no document body
With no embedding provider configured, a search returns its lexical (BM25) results rather than erroring or returning empty
On the golden fixture corpus, identifier and exact-term queries return the recorded expected top hit first, ranked by the `pg_search` BM25 index with the identifier/exact-term boost
Lexical ranking is served by the Postgres `pg_search` index; no in-memory or hand-rolled BM25 implementation exists
On the two-project fixture, results contain only hits from the current project scope and never hits from the other project
Results expose lexical signal contribution
BM25 remains available when semantic search is disabled or failing
Batches dispatch grouped by provider, model, and dimension, dispatch stops when the FR-029 budget reservation is refused, and failed dispatches are reported for retry
Over-budget degradation carries the `RETR_NOTE_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED` note code from the FR-028 registry
OpenAI egress requires explicit provider settings, model, and stored key reference; without them no OpenAI request is issued

On the fusion-divergent fixture, a lexical-heavy weight configuration ranks the lexical-best hit first and a vector-heavy configuration ranks the vector-best hit first: changing weights verifiably flips the observable ranking
A request with `top_k` above the maximum returns exactly the maximum (100) hits, clamped without error
A hit whose vector similarity equals the configured threshold contributes its vector signal; a hit strictly below the threshold contributes none

A hit whose stored vector content hash differs from the current content hash carries `RETR_NOTE_STALE_SEMANTIC`, and its vector contribution is excluded or halved according to the configured stale-vector handling mode
On the controlled-timestamp fixture with a nonzero recency weight, a newer document ranks above an otherwise signal-equal older document, and setting the recency weight to zero removes the effect

Every degradation and egress note carries a `code` from the note registry matching its cause; a test double forcing each degradation cause yields exactly the registered code, and an unregistered or empty code fails

Every `RETR_NOTE_` string in the workspace is a member of the registry and no module other than Retrieval declares one; the repository source-scan gate fails on an unregistered literal or an out-of-module declaration
Every registered code round-trips the registry lookup, and constructing a note with an unregistered or empty code is rejected

An empty result whose candidates were all removed by the request's target filters carries `RETR_NOTE_FILTERS_EXCLUDED_ALL`; an empty result from a query that matched nothing, and any non-empty result, do not
Chunking the same content twice yields byte-identical chunk sets within the size and overlap bounds
Re-enqueueing content whose (content hash, chunk index) already has a pending or in-flight job creates no duplicate job, and pending jobs dispatch in FIFO order

A failing job retries with exponential backoff at most 3 times and then remains failed-retryable with a diagnostic; every observed state change is a permitted lifecycle transition and no forbidden transition occurs
After an index run in which content changed and content was deleted, changed-content jobs are cancelled and re-enqueued under the new hash and deleted-content jobs are marked stale and cancelled
Concurrent batches reserving estimated tokens never exceed the per-provider per-project daily budget in total, and reported actual usage replaces estimates in the ledger
While the code layer is indexed alongside the spec layer, embedding enqueue selects only spec-layer documents; source-layer documents are never enqueued
Every page is bounded by the effective page size and pages arrive in stable key order
Following `next_cursor` to exhaustion yields every project graph node and edge exactly once, with totals matching the delivered counts
Non-project targets, cross-project scopes, and malformed cursors return corrective errors before graph rows are read
A request that does not ask for chunked delivery, or one whose transport cannot carry it, receives the requested single page unchanged from the paged form
A streamed traversal and a paged traversal of one unchanged scope deliver the same rows in the same order, each exactly once, with matching totals
Resuming the paged form from a mid-stream chunk's `next_cursor` yields the remainder exactly once, with no row delivered twice

A request naming no layer exports the spec layer only; naming both layers exports both plus the cross-layer edges between them; naming one layer excludes cross-layer edges whose other endpoint is unexported; and a widened export still pages to exhaustion delivering every row exactly once
A folder root returns the artifacts declared beneath it with code, title, type, and path, ordered by path then code
A folder root does not enumerate a sibling folder sharing its name as a prefix, and excludes code-layer artifacts
A listing cut by `limit` reports the unbounded total, the truncation, and the bound applied
An `artifact_types` filter returns only entries of the named types; an empty type name is rejected
A request with no target enumerates the whole authorized project scope
An `artifact_types` entry matching nothing under the root is reported back; entries that matched are not
An artifact target returns the declaring document's frontmatter and body, plus the artifact's code, title, and type
A document target returns that document's frontmatter and body, and omits the artifact identity fields
A body longer than the ceiling is returned as a valid-UTF-8 prefix and reported as truncated
`metadata_only` returns frontmatter and identity with no body field
A target holding no indexed content returns a corrective error naming an addressable alternative, not an empty success
A search request without `layers` returns results identical to the pre-change behavior on a mixed-layer corpus, and contains zero code-layer rows
`layers: ["code"]` returns code artifact and graph-node hits by symbol name and returns no spec rows; code document bodies never match
`layers: ["spec","code"]` ranks both layers with per-layer lexical normalization: each layer's top hit normalizes against its own layer maximum
`layers: []` is refused with a registered parameter error naming the closed set
An unknown layers member or an unknown parameter field is refused, not ignored
A code-only query's plan uses the code-layer partial indexes (no sequential scan of spec rows)
The CLI accepts `search --layers spec,code` and the MCP search tool accepts the same field through its free-form params
A document hit's excerpt contains a term from the query and is not equal to the hit's `target.path`
Every excerpt is at most 300 Unicode scalar values, splits no character, and contains no highlight markup or tag characters around matched terms

A document hit's `line` is the 1-based line of its matched span within the fixture document's body, counted from the file's first line including frontmatter, and does not move when the excerpt bound changes
A document hit's `heading` is the enclosing Markdown heading chain for the matched span's line, outermost first, each heading carrying its text without `#` markers
A hit that resolves to no owning document still carries its identity, and omits `line`, `heading`, and the excerpt rather than emitting zero or empty values
An artifact hit and a graph-node hit each return the matched field's own value as the excerpt
A vector-matched hit returns the matched chunk's text as its excerpt

The lexical search SQL bounds each matching branch with its own score-ordered limit before excerpting, so that excerpt and locator computation is evaluated for at most `top_k` rows per branch rather than for the full match set
A hit whose match lies in the document's frontmatter returns the frontmatter region as its excerpt, and a hit for which no excerpt can be drawn omits the excerpt rather than returning an empty string
An artifact hit carries its `code`, `title`, and `type`, and its excerpt is the owning document's description — equal to none of the three
A graph-node hit carries the `code`, `title`, and `type` of the object it names, taken from the node's extracted data, and its name is returned without any reference or path prefix
A document whose body has no `## Description` section yields its first prose paragraph as the description, and a document with one yields that section
An artifact hit's `line` is the line of the heading opening that artifact's section, not the line of its frontmatter identifier

metrics.name: coverage.backed
metrics.method: rows of the declared reference tables whose trace target is bound by at least one source symbol; `matched` counts the evidence symbols that bound a trace id out of the `examined` evidence symbols walked, so matched 0 of a non-zero examined is a ratio computed over a corpus the binder could not read

metrics.name: authoring.tag_rate
metrics.method: evidence symbols whose attached annotation block carries an id-shaped token, whether or not the declared trace grammar can read it; `value` counts tagged symbols, while `matched` counts candidates classified as tagged or untagged so an honest zero is not mistaken for an unread population

metrics.name: coverage.self_named_binding.rust
metrics.method: evidence symbols carrying a separator-delimited id in their own declaration name whose id was read by a declared name form; comment and attribute bindings do not satisfy this premise

metrics.name: coverage.self_named_binding.typescript
metrics.method: evidence symbols carrying a separator-delimited id in their own declaration name whose id was read by a declared name form; comment and attribute bindings do not satisfy this premise

metrics.name: coverage.property_shaped
metrics.method: criteria the FR-052 classifier reads a property shape from
metrics.because: no corpus document in scope binds an acceptance criterion, so nothing was classified

metrics.name: coverage.specific_shaped
metrics.method: extractable criteria whose shape names what property to write
metrics.because: no corpus document in scope binds an acceptance criterion, so nothing was classified

metrics.name: coverage.no_symbol_rows
metrics.method: unbacked rows whose declared test type is in the module's `no_source_symbol` vocabulary, counted over every row reconciled

metrics.name: coverage.implements
metrics.method: production symbols carrying at least one declared `implements` marker, counted over the production symbols examined; a zero means none is annotated, not that none was read

metrics.name: minting.section_hit_rate
metrics.method: documents whose declared `section:` heading was found, over the documents a required trace target's `archetype:` selected and its `exclude:` kept, plus documents where an optional target's section was present; counted per (trace target, document) pair. An optional absent section is outside the population. A required miss reads the archetype right and the heading wrong, so the whole table is stranded and its ids never enter `coverage.backed`'s denominator at all

metrics.name: authoring.tag_rate
metrics.method: evidence symbols whose attached annotation block carries an id-shaped token, whether or not the declared trace grammar can read it; `value` counts tagged symbols, while `matched` counts candidates classified as tagged or untagged so an honest zero is not mistaken for an unread population

metrics.name: coverage.backed
metrics.method: rows of the declared reference tables whose trace target is bound by at least one source symbol; `matched` counts the evidence symbols that bound a trace id out of the `examined` evidence symbols walked, so matched 0 of a non-zero examined is a ratio computed over a corpus the binder could not read

metrics.name: coverage.implements
metrics.method: production symbols carrying at least one declared `implements` marker, counted over the production symbols examined; a zero means none is annotated, not that none was read

metrics.name: coverage.no_symbol_rows
metrics.method: unbacked rows whose declared test type is in the module's `no_source_symbol` vocabulary, counted over every row reconciled

metrics.name: coverage.property_shaped
metrics.method: criteria the FR-052 classifier reads a property shape from
metrics.because: no corpus document in scope binds an acceptance criterion, so nothing was classified

metrics.name: coverage.self_named_binding.rust
metrics.method: evidence symbols carrying a separator-delimited id in their own declaration name whose id was read by a declared name form; comment and attribute bindings do not satisfy this premise

metrics.name: coverage.self_named_binding.typescript
metrics.method: evidence symbols carrying a separator-delimited id in their own declaration name whose id was read by a declared name form; comment and attribute bindings do not satisfy this premise

metrics.name: coverage.specific_shaped
metrics.method: extractable criteria whose shape names what property to write
metrics.because: no corpus document in scope binds an acceptance criterion, so nothing was classified

metrics.name: minting.section_hit_rate
metrics.method: documents whose declared `section:` heading was found, over the documents a required trace target's `archetype:` selected and its `exclude:` kept, plus documents where an optional target's section was present; counted per (trace target, document) pair. An optional absent section is outside the population. A required miss reads the archetype right and the heading wrong, so the whole table is stranded and its ids never enter `coverage.backed`'s denominator at all
